newsitem.title: CHINA: Haixing sees better second half results.
newsitem.headline: Haixing sees better second half results.

text.p: Shanghai Haixing Shipping, China's second biggest shipping firm, said on Friday it expected better results in the second half of 1996 but declined to predict a return to profitability after a big first half loss.
The Hong Kong-listed company last month reported a loss of 84.5 million yuan for the first half of the year compared to a profit of 50.5 million yuan in the same period last year.
The secretary to the board of directors, Ye Yuwang, said in an interview on Friday that the loss was largely the result of increased provisions for bad debts.

"The national economic situation is improving and the cut in bank interest rates in May and last month have helped, but I am not in a position to say whether or not the company will be in profit or loss for 1996 as a whole," he said.
"The interest rate cut particularly helps to stimulate industry and other economic development and will eventually affect the energy shipping market, but there is a time-lag," Ye said.
"Pressures on our business from increasing costs and other factors will remain big for the rest of 1996 and 1997," he said.

He said the company had sold three ships in the first half of this year and its hopes of moving back into profit depended on how many more ships could be sold in the second half. None have been sold to date.

The company, which has 180 ships on its books, took delivery of two new vessels in the first half and has taken delivery of one in the second half. Two other container ships due for delivery in the second half of the year might be delayed until 1997, he said.
Ye said the company hoped for a breakthrough in discussions between China and Taiwan on direct trade, which he said would be a very positive factor for Haixing, but he added:
"I don't expect any movement on that this year."
